what: 8.4 Interpreter sharing — the real design question
title: nat.python — plan
text: reticulate binds exactly one Python interpreter per R session: package triggers initialisation, interpreter environment fixed R restarts. several consumers (fafbseg, seatabler, bancr) live one session choose Python, someone must single, deterministic resolution. Decision: (C). Alternatives, (C) adopted: () Leave env management consumer. Rejected. fafbseg seatabler race initialise Python disagree env; whoever imports first silently wins. status quo’s latent bug, worsened consumers. (B) nat.python owns one managed env, eagerly. single simple_python-style env holds everything (cloudvolume + caveclient + seatable_api + …). Simple close today, monolithic: every package must co-resolve one env (existing seatable_api!=2.6.3 pin exactly conflict), spins Python even sessions never need . respects user-configured Python first — RETICULATE_PYTHON, active venv/conda, explicit reticulate::use_* — falls back managed miniconda env (generalising fafbseg’s existing ownpythonrequested / checkownpython); reuses existing env name/path (default_pyenv) current fafbseg users saddled second multi-GB environment; initialises lazily (delay_load) merely loading consumer package start Python; diagnoses rather enforces — interpreter swapped mid-session, missing module yields clear “active Python X; module Y absent; run simple_python(...)” (via py_report), silent re-initialisation attempt.

title: Ensure a Python module is installed and importable — check_module
text: generic gate code needs particular Python module: checks module installed, imports , optionally enforces minimum version, — missing — either installs (interactively request) errors actionable guidance. Package-specific checks (fafbseg's check_seatable() / check_cloudvolume_reticulate()) become thin wrappers .

title: Ensure a Python module is installed and importable — check_module
code: check_module(   module,   package = module,   min_version = NULL,   install = c("ask", "never", "always"),   install_cmd = "none",   docs_url = NULL,   cache = TRUE )

title: Ensure a Python module is installed and importable — check_module
text: module single Python module (import) name, e.g. "seatable_api". package pip package (distribution) name install module missing. Defaults module; supply differ (e.g. import "cv2" package "opencv-python"). min_version Optional minimum acceptable version (character numeric_version). Checked every call via module_version(). install handle missing module: "ask" (default) prompts interactive session otherwise errors; "never" always errors install instructions; "always" installs without prompting. install_cmd bundle argument passed simple_python() installing (default "none", .e. install package). Use e.g. "basic" pull whole ecosystem bundle instead. docs_url Optional documentation URL added failure message. cache Whether use (populate) session cache results (default TRUE). Pass FALSE force fresh check — e.g. installing upgrading module band.

title: Ensure a Python module is installed and importable — check_module
text: check deliberately ordered installed-first, load-second, two failure modes need different advice. Installation detected Python distribution metadata via py_module_info() (import module), falling back reticulate::py_module_available() namespace/local packages lack metadata. module known installed actually imported, import fails reported load problem (broken mismatched environment), distinct package simply absent — underlying Python error surfaced. result memoised session, repeated calls module cheap hand back already-imported module object. installation via simple_python() clears cache (well module_version() cache), next call re-checks picks newly installed package. , package-specific wrappers need memoise .

title: Convert a pandas DataFrame to an R data frame — pandas2df
text: x pandas DataFrame (reticulate pandas.core.frame.DataFrame). use_arrow TRUE, convert via temporary Feather file using arrow package rather memory. Implies tibble result. keep_index Whether keep pandas index column. tibble Whether return tibble rather base data frame. Defaults use_arrow. bigint represent integer columns. "auto" (default) maps column narrowest faithful base R type: values fitting 32-bit R integer become integer, larger values 2^53 become double (exact), values 2^53 signed 64-bit maximum become bit64::integer64 – reserving integer64 base R hold exactly. "integer64" returns every integer column bit64::integer64 stable schema regardless magnitude. "character" behaves like "auto" returns large (>= 2^53) tier character, data.table::fread() offers. uint64 values beyond signed 64-bit range held integer64; always returned character, warning unless bigint = "character".

title: Convert a pandas DataFrame to an R data frame — pandas2df

Genuine list-valued columns (e.g. multi-select values) left intact. datetime columns normalised POSIXct UTC. optional use_arrow path round-trips Feather file needs Suggested arrow package; bigint apply .
